statements.t: The Company believes its existing and planned facilities are suitable, adequate, and have sufficient capacity to support current operations and anticipated near-term business needs.
For full-year 2026, the Company remains on track to achieve an increase of approximately 200,000 to 400,000 FDM units, compared with 2025.

These programs are expected to continue growing through 2026 and into 2027, supporting the Company’s previously communicated target of approximately $80 million to $100 million of DMS and ICMS revenue in 2027.
The Company has entered into a lease agreement and continues development activities toward a targeted start of production during the fourth quarter of 2027.

Development of the Company’s dimmable visor remains on track for an initial start of production in the fourth quarter of 2027, while work continues with additional OEMs on product design and validation for potential future awards.
During the third quarter of 2026, the Company secured its first printed circuit board assembly (“PCBA”) business award, with production currently expected to begin in 2029.
The Company is also actively pursuing additional PCBA manufacturing opportunities with anticipated production timelines beginning in or around the same period.
The Company expects to continue investing in business development, engineering, manufacturing planning, and other activities necessary to support potential future contract manufacturing programs.

As vehicles become increasingly connected and software-defined, the Company intends to leverage its installed automotive platforms and expertise in electronics, connectivity, sensing, and identity technologies to develop additional features and services within and beyond the vehicle.
During 2026, the Company was awarded its first production program for its Dimmable Sun Visor technology, with start of production currently expected in 2027.
The Company is currently experiencing increased costs and supply constraints for certain memory products and other electronic components, which are expected to continue into 2027.
There can be no assurance that the Company will be successful in fully offsetting these pressures.

The Company's light vehicle production forecasts for the fourth quarter of 2026 and full years 2026 and 2027, are based on the mid-Oct 2026 Mobility Global outlook for North America, Europe, Japan/Korea, and China (see table below).

While global light vehicle production is expected to increase approximately 1% in 2027, the Company anticipates continued weakness in its primary automotive markets of North America, Europe, and Japan/Korea.

Based on actual results for the first nine months of 2026, the updated Mobility Global light vehicle production forecast, and the Company's current expectations for its Automotive, Premium Audio, and Other product categories, the Company is updating certain elements of its full-year 2026 guidance, as outlined below.

Based on the mid‑Oct 2026 Mobility Global light‑vehicle production forecast and the Company’s current expectations for Automotive, Premium Audio, and Other Products revenue, the Company is maintaining its calendar-year 2027 revenue outlook of $2.80 billion to $2.90 billion.
This outlook assumes light vehicle production in the Company's primary markets declines approximately 1% in 2027.

Automotive unit performance during the quarter was consistent with expectations; however, revenue for the quarter was approximately $35 million below the Company's forecast at the beginning of the quarter due to certain customer issues and delayed launches in the quarter.

“Despite continued challenges in China and Europe, we delivered third quarter net sales that were relatively flat compared to the third quarter of 2025 even though revenue was approximately $35 million below our beginning-of-quarter forecast.

The team also continues to move our large area device R&D project closer to a qualified product, with a volume manufacturing footprint that can scale to support the significant volume we are expecting from customers once the product is fully validated,” concluded Boehm.
Automotive revenue performance during the quarter reflected expected unit trends and strong content growth across the Company’s primary markets.

The Company intends to continue to repurchase additional shares of its common stock in support of the previously disclosed capital allocation strategy, but share repurchases will vary from time to time and will take into account macroeconomic issues, market trends, and other factors that the Company deems appropriate.
The Company’s light vehicle production assumptions are based on the mid-October 2026 Mobility Global outlook.

Global light vehicle production is expected to increase approximately 1% in 2027, compared to 2026; however, production in the Company’s primary automotive markets of North America, Europe, and Japan/Korea is forecasted to decline approximately 1%, with growth concentrated in China and other markets.

Based on actual results for the first nine months of 2026, the updated Mobility Global light vehicle production forecast, and the Company’s expectations for its Automotive, Premium Audio, and Other Products categories, the Company is updating certain elements of its full-year 2026 guidance as set forth below.

Based on the mid-October 2026 Mobility Global light vehicle production forecast and the Company’s current expectations for Automotive, Premium Audio, and Other Products revenue, the Company is maintaining its 2027 revenue outlook of $2.80 billion to $2.90 billion.
This outlook assumes light vehicle production in the Company’s primary markets declines approximately 1% in 2027.
“We are beginning to see the impact of our broader product and growth strategy reflected in our forward-looking guidance.

Despite a light vehicle production environment in our primary markets that is currently expected to decline approximately 1% in 2027, we are maintaining our 2027 revenue outlook of $2.80 billion to $2.90 billion, which is a significant acceleration in outgrowth versus the underlying market.
We are also pleased to announce that during the third quarter we secured our first PCBA business award, with production currently expected to begin in 2029.

This award represents another important opportunity to leverage Gentex’s advanced manufacturing capabilities in new products and markets, and we are actively pursuing additional PCBA opportunities with anticipated production timelines beginning in or around the same period.
And while these cost headwinds are expected to continue into the fourth quarter, our teams are actively engaged with our customers to establish the need for appropriate reimbursement.
